 Intel employees report new IT layoffs as restructuring continues
 The company's latest reported headcount stood at 81,100 in September, down from 88,400 a year earlier. Employee accounts now point to further reductions in its information technology organization.
 CTech 09:22, 18.11.26 Intel employees have reported a new round of job cuts targeting the chipmaker's global information technology organization, adding to a prolonged restructuring drive that has steadily reduced the company's workforce across the United States and international operations. The reported cuts began on November 16, although their scale and geographic reach remain unclear. The reports come as CEO Lip-Bu Tan continues efforts to streamline operations and reduce costs at the struggling semiconductor company. Intel has been cutting jobs and reorganizing its business as it attempts to improve efficiency and refocus its operations. In response to questions about the reported reductions, an Intel spokesperson did not provide a headcount or identify the teams affected. "As part of our broader strategy to become a more focused and efficient company, we continually assess our workforce to ensure priorities and resources are appropriately aligned," the company said. The statement did not explicitly confirm a new round of layoffs. 1 View gallery Intel. ( Photo: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg ) Accounts posted on employee discussion platforms described cuts within Intel's global IT organization. One post claimed that the reductions were concentrated in IT and represented a double-digit percentage of the department's workforce, although it did not provide a verified number. Other accounts described individual employees receiving notifications that their positions had been eliminated. The reported IT reductions would follow a series of smaller workforce cuts and organizational changes at Intel during 2026. In July, the company reduced staff within its Data Center and AI Group. Between July and October, Intel filed nine separate Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) notices in California covering a total of 222 employees. The most recent of those notices, filed on October 22, covered 67 permanent layoffs at Intel's Folsom, California, campus, with an effective date of October 31. Earlier filings in July and September covered additional reductions at facilities in Santa Clara. No new Intel WARN filing had appeared by November 17, although the absence of a notice does not establish that no smaller or internationally based reductions took place.  Intel's overall workforce has continued to shrink. According to the company's third-quarter financial results, its total headcount stood at 81,100 as of September 26, comprising 76,500 employees at Intel and 4,600 at Mobileye and other subsidiaries. That was 4,000 fewer employees than at the end of 2025, when the company reported a workforce of 85,100, and 7,300 fewer than a year earlier, when the total stood at 88,400. The workforce reductions come as Intel faces renewed pressure from investors. Its shares closed at $55.17 on November 17, following a difficult stretch for the stock. Among the latest developments weighing on sentiment was a regulatory filing showing that Nvidia reduced its Intel holdings by 25% during the third quarter, cutting its position from approximately 214.8 million shares to 161.1 million. Intel is also facing a proposed shareholder class-action lawsuit filed in federal court in San Jose. The case, led by Michigan's City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System, alleges that Intel executives failed to disclose in a timely manner how weakening personal computer demand and excess inventory would affect the company's financial performance. The lawsuit also names Tan and Chief Financial Officer David Zinsner. The allegations have not been proven, and Intel had not responded to Reuters' request for comment when the lawsuit was reported.
